title: Split environment provider bindings and introduce provider profiles for workspace stability
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Refactor Terraform provisioning so provider configuration is surfaced via deterministic per-environment provider profiles instead of ad-hoc workspace-side provider overrides. Goal is to reduce non-deterministic plan/apply failures caused by mixed provider versions and to enable faster parallel plans across multiple workspaces.
acceptance_criteria: Introduce provider profile concept and config file (provider_profiles.yml) referenced by each environment overlay
CI runs plan/apply in parallel for at least three staging workspaces without provider init conflicts
Provider plugin versions are pinned per-profile and documented in the upgrade matrix
Rollback plan exists to revert to global provider pinning within two hours if a production apply fails
tasks: Draft provider_profiles.yml schema and example for aws/azurerm/aws-lambda modules
Update module interfaces to accept provider aliasing and explicit provider versions
Implement provider-init wrapper in infra-ci to initialize a profile-specific plugin cache directory
Run smoke tests on staging (eu-west-1, us-east-1) with 3 parallel plans
Create migration script to convert existing workspaces to profiles; dry-run in dev env
technical_notes: We will move from a single global .terraform/plugins.lock to per-profile locks to avoid plugin checksum mismatches
Terraform 1.6+ remains minimum; leverage the -plugin-dir flag for isolated plugin caches
Some legacy overlays assume implicit provider lookup; modules must be made explicit with provider = aws.some_alias to avoid drift
This reduces tf init churn by isolating plugin downloads per-profile and enables safe provider upgrades via staged profile rollouts

migration_plan: Stage 1: create provider_profiles.yml for dev workspaces and validate plan/apply (2 days)
Stage 2: roll out profiles to staging clusters and run parallel plans (3 days)
Stage 3: incrementally adopt in production on low-risk environments (canary) and monitor TF state drift (2 days)
Rollback: restore previous provider lock files from artifact store and re-run tf init with global plugin cache
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: module consumers still use implicit provider lookups leading to ambiguous provider selection; Mitigation: add CI linter that fails if modules use implicit providers
Risk: provider upgrade causes API incompatibility in networking modules; Mitigation: stage upgrades behind provider profile versions and run e2e network tests
